2607.20902.title: Anti-Goal Reasoning: Rethinking the Theory of Goal Reasoning in Non-Axiomatic Logic
2607.20902.paper_summary: Goal reasoning in Non-Axiomatic Logic (NAL) explains how an adaptive system derives means for realizing desired events under insufficient knowledge and resources. However, the representation of avoidance is less clear. A common convention is to express ``avoid $G$'' as the goal sentence ``$\neg G!$'', but this notation conflates two different readings: pursuing the negated event $\neg G$, and avoiding the positive event $G$. This paper shows that the conflation can produce a paradoxical case in which an avoidance intention is converted into a positive goal to act merely because acting is usually followed by the absence of hurt. Starting from NAL's basic definition of goals, the framework is extended with a corresponding definition of anti-goals, so that avoidance can be represented without treating it as the pursuit of a negated event. Finally, a mental operation, $\op{prevent}$, is introduced to connect anti-goal reasoning with ordinary goal reasoning in cases of active prevention. Four minimal case studies check that the resulting rules distinguish pursuit, passive avoidance, active prevention, and withholding action to preserve a desired event.
2607.20902.paper_summary_zh: 目標推理在非公理邏輯（NAL）中解釋了適應系統如何在知識和資源不足的情況下推導出實現期望事件的手段。<lb/>然而，避免的表達則不太清晰。一個常見的慣例是將「避免 $G$」表達為目標句「$\neg G!$」，但這種符號將兩種不同的解讀混淆在一起：追求被否定的事件 $\neg G$，以及避免正面的事件 $G$。<lb/>本文顯示，這種混淆可能產生一種矛盾的情況，其中避免意圖被轉化為一個正面的行動目標，僅僅因為行動通常會隨之而來的是沒有傷害。<lb/>從 NAL 對目標的基本定義出發，該框架擴展了反目標的相應定義，以便在不將避免視為追求否定事件的情況下進行表達。<lb/>最後，引入了一種心理操作 $\op{prevent}$，以將反目標推理與普通目標推理聯繫起來，適用於主動預防的情況。<lb/>四個最小案例研究檢查了所產生的規則是否能區分追求、被動避免、主動預防以及保留行動以維護期望事件。
2607.20902.author: Bowen Xu et.al.
